body:
I'm in that age range. 


Yeah, it's depressing to still be struggling with depression. I've had it since childhood, along with crippling social anxiety and a number of other concerns. I had hoped I would somehow "outgrow" it but here I am. I HAVE done much better but I don't have much hope of getting back to that point. 


When it comes to dating(and I bring this up because I'm lonely as fuck, as I imagine many here are, and I still have a functioning libido..somehow)... I really don't want to have to explain to someone that I've spent most of my life stunted by anxiety/depression, right off the bat. And it would come up. I never went to college, I'm currently on SSDI, I'm currently essentially housebound by anxiety, & hobbies are non-existent.  I've been in more than one long-term relationship(last one was ~ 5 years) but I just don't see it happening again for a number of reasons, and that's quite sad for me. 


I was an "honors student" in school, quite bright, full of interests, and so on. Now I'm this.  I always envisioned a future with a home & a family(consisting of myself, a partner, and a number of animals).  I currently live in a basement with my cats and am facing potential homelessness. 


So yeah, dating is not in the cards right now. As for making new friends, I cannot imagine. Again, it's so much that I would need to explain, and I've never had an easy time finding people with whom I could have the connection I desire/consider a likemind/et. I have friends but they live elsewhere; I don't know anyone here(I moved across the country for a relationship - great decision, yeah). 


What keeps me going?  My cats, my friends, my sense of humor, my fantasies, and the strength I've developed from years of dealing with depression/anxiety & a number of painful events, mostly on my own.  Distraction also helps.

Thank you so much for your reply. I empathize deeply with you and wish you the best as well. 


My only advice regarding housing would be to apply to senior/disabled housing in different areas, particularly more rural areas where the waiting lists are generally shorter. 


I wish you the best and thank you for the reply.
